If $49 \cos (3 \mathrm{C})+42=\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{n}}$, where $\operatorname{gcd}(\mathrm{m}, \mathrm{n})=1$, then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to________

$S = \dfrac{a + b + c}{2}$⇒ S = 6k$

questions.q: Let in a right angled triangle, the smallest angle be $\theta .$ If a triangle formed by taking the reciprocal of its sides is also a right angled triangle, then $sin\theta$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $A = \theta$, then $B = 90 ° - \theta$.

Hence, $a$ is the smallest side.

Then, in $∆ ACB$

${c}^{2} = {a}^{2} + {b}^{2}$

On taking reciprocal, longest side become shortest and vice versa.

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{{a}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{{b}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{c}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{b}^{2}{c}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} = {b}^{2} + {c}^{2} . . . \left(i\right)$

Use $a = 2RsinA = 2Rsin\theta$

$b = 2RsinB = 2Rsin ( 90 ° - \theta ) = 2Rcos\theta$

$c = 2RsinC = 2sin90 ° = 2R$

Hence, by $\left(i\right)$

$\dfrac{4{R}^{2}\cos^{2}\theta \cdot 4{R}^{2}}{4{R}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta} = 4{R}^{2}\cos^{2}\theta + 4{R}^{2}$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \sin^{2}\theta\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta$

$⇒ 1 - \sin^{2}\theta = \sin^{2}\theta\left(1 - \sin^{2}\theta\right) + \sin^{2}\theta$

$⇒ 1 = 3\sin^{2}\theta - \sin^{4}\theta$

$⇒ \sin^{4}\theta - 3\sin^{2}\theta + 1 = 0$

$⇒ \sin^{2}\theta = \dfrac{3 - \sqrt{5}}{2} = \dfrac{5 + 1 - 2\sqrt{5}}{4} = {\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{5} - 1}{2}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ sin\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{5} - 1}{2}$

questions.q: If in a triangle $ABC, AB = 5$ units, $∠ B = \cos^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)$ and radius of circumcircle of $∆ ABC$ is $5$ units, then the area (in sq. units) of $\DeltaABC$ is:
questions.solution:
We have,

As,

$cosB = \dfrac{3}{5} ⇒ sinB = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Given:

$R = 5$

By sine rule, we have

$\dfrac{c}{sinC} = 2R$

$⇒ \dfrac{5}{10} = sinC$

$⇒ C = 30 °$
Now,

$\dfrac{b}{sinB} = 2R$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{4}{5} \times 10 = 8$

Now, by cosine formula

$cosB = \dfrac{{a}^{2} + {c}^{2} - {b}^{2}}{2ac}$

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{{a}^{2} + 25 - 64}{2\left(5\right)a}$

$⇒ {a}^{2} - 6a - 39 = 0$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{192}}{2} = \dfrac{6 \pm 8\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$⇒ a = \left(3 + 4\sqrt{3}\right)$

(Reject $a = 3 - 4\sqrt{3} < 0$)

Now, $\Delta = \dfrac{abc}{4R} = \dfrac{\left(3 + 4\sqrt{3}\right) \cdot 8 \cdot 5}{4 \cdot 5} = 2\left(3 + 4\sqrt{3}\right)$

$⇒ \Delta = \left(6 + 8\sqrt{3}\right)$ sq. units.

questions.q: The angles $A, B \text{ and } C$ of a $∆ ABC$ are in $A . P .$ and $a: b = 1: \sqrt{3} .$ If $c = 4cm,$ then the area (in $sq . cm$) of this triangle is:
questions.solution:
In $∆ ABC,$ angles $A, B, C$ are in $A . P .$ hence $2 ∠ B = ∠ A + ∠ C$

Also, by angle sum property $∠ A + ∠ B + ∠ C = 180 °$

$⇒ 2 ∠ B + ∠ B = 180 °$

$⇒ ∠B = 60 ° .$

Now $a: b = 1: \sqrt{3}$

By, using sine rule, we have $\dfrac{sinA}{a} = \dfrac{sinB}{b} = \dfrac{sinC}{c}$

$⇒ \dfrac{sinA}{a} = \dfrac{sinB}{b}$

$⇒ \dfrac{sinA}{sin\left(60 °\right)} = \dfrac{a}{b}$

$⇒ sinA = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ ∠ A = 30 °$ and hence $∠ C = 90 °$

Thus, the triangle $ABC$ is a right triangle, with hypotenuse $AB = 4cm .$

Again, by Sine rule, we have $\dfrac{sin\left(30 °\right)}{a} = \dfrac{sin\left(60 °\right)}{b} = \dfrac{sin\left(90 °\right)}{4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{a} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)}{b} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2a} = \dfrac{1}{4}$ and $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2b} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ a = 2cm$ and $b = 2\sqrt{3}cm$

Now, the area of $∆ ABC = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(base\right) \times \left(height\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(a \cdot b\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 2\sqrt{3} = 2\sqrt{3}sq . cm .$

questions.q: If the lengths of the sides of a triangle are in A.P and the greatest angle is double the smallest, then a ratio of lengths of the sides of this triangle is:
questions.solution:
Let $a < b < c$ are three sides and $\theta$ is the smallest angle. Hence three angles are $\theta, \pi - 3\theta, 2\theta$
Given, $2b = a + c ⇒ 2sin ⁡ B = sin ⁡ A + sin ⁡ C$ (using sine rule)
$⇒ 2sin3\theta = sin\theta + sin2\theta$
$⇒ 2\left(3sin\theta - 4\sin^{3}\theta\right) = sin\theta\left(1 + 2cos\theta\right)$
$⇒ 6 - 8\left(1 - \cos^{2}\theta\right) = 1 + 2cos\theta$
$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{3}{4}, - \dfrac{1}{2}$ ( $- \dfrac{1}{2}$ is rejected since $\theta$ is acute)
$∴ a: b: c = sinA: sinB: sinC = sin\theta: sin3\theta: sin2\theta$
$= 1: 3 - 4\sin^{2}\theta: 2cos\theta = 1: 4\cos^{2}\theta - 1: 2cos\theta$
$= 4: 5: 6$

$= 4: 5: 6$
